title: Unconquerable Heroine
text: “By the way, the spirit with the strongest dose of toxin mixed in around here was the Shield Spirit. I was panicking at the time, but well… by the stage where I was selecting Naofumi Iwatani-kun, it was fine.”
“I agree that trust in Father is warranted, but is there something specific behind that, I wonder?”
“That’s… well, it touches on something you know you’re not supposed to talk about. Remember that prophecy?”
Ugh… so Father has some things he’s not supposed to speak of, indeed. If it touches on that, I suppose it’s better not to ask further.
“More importantly, there’s no doubt the Shield Spirit has the best compatibility for linking up with Naofumi Iwatani as a holder—speaking purely in terms of compatibility.”
“Ark did make use of you once, did it not?”

“That was closer to an exception-handling case. That accessory was the medium, after all. Still, the power I got at the same time was pretty impressive, you know? Honestly, that alone boosted my strength considerably. Well, it’s more like I received power that had been donated to help strengthen Master Ark.”
What exactly are you bragging about?
“Anyway, back to the topic—combining power with the spirit-kind let me put out strength close to a Hero’s, didn’t it? In this loop.”
Ah, yes, in later years that sort of technique spread widely, indeed. Research into species capable of that progressed all across the world.
“In other words, once this loop took shape, it became a world where spirits were born more easily. It had been a lost technique, you see.”
In worlds touched by whoever triggered the Waves, cases of becoming a spirit had grown terribly rare, which caused no end of trouble. Or so the Spear Spirit continued, indeed.
“So yeah, the evaluation of this loop, which turned out rather nicely, is extremely high.”
“What I can dimly recall is… up until around the point the Queen became some kind of blazer-wearing warrior, I believe.”
I can vaguely recall things happening after that too, but it’s all getting rather hazy now, indeed.

“Needless to say, after that, once the Waves ended, the world became peaceful. The Bow Hero’s exploits and various other things happened along the way. Then research into spirit-kind advanced, and the whole field of spirit technology developed. Quite a few unexpected turns, wouldn’t you say?”
“What became of Rafumi, then?”
“It came out that she was a spirit quite a few years later. She let it slip herself, more or less. She could come to this realm too, technically, but she hasn’t yet.”
The Spear Spirit glanced around, searching for Rafumi, indeed.
“Imiya griped about it a fair amount too, watching on and saying, ‘don’t you dare pile that kind of burden on the me of back then,’ I recall.”
And it let out a snicker, mocking me with a laugh just like Itsuki’s, how irritating.
“If Rafumi’s technology has advanced that much, she should just let herself be dissected, indeed.”

“I won’t let it get that far. Besides, research that desecrates spirits isn’t permitted, so it’s a fairly livable world for spirits on the whole… though spirits aren’t a monolith either, so whether some might fall to evil is still a worry.”
“I rather thought spirits were more like absolute justice incarnate.”
“Don’t overestimate us… well, I doubt it’ll happen, but even being a spirit doesn’t mean there are no problems at all, that much is true.”
“By the way, what became of Father in this loop?”

No matter how hard I try to remember, only hazy fragments come to me, indeed. Did he end up united with Big Sister? I have some vague feeling he got along well with Older Sister and Panda too… ugh, and images keep surfacing of him standing alongside Crocodile Guy, Rabbit Guy, and Wolf and the others.
“Now, how was that again, I wonder? If you’re so worried, why don’t you marry him yourself?”
Gah… this homo spirit!
“Father is normal, indeed!”
“Still going on about that… honestly, I wish you’d just get on with making things official already. You’ve got better odds with him than with Filo-chan, who seems utterly unconquerable.”
“Filo-tan and I are destined to marry someday, indeed!”

I bring peace to the world day and night precisely so that I might one day earn Father’s blessing, indeed! Sometimes I’m not sure just how much peace is enough, but even a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step, indeed. In my mind, Father—who never managed to save me from this—remarks that I’m basically running endlessly toward the moon in some pointless act, but surely that’s just my imagination.
“Wow… the sheer conviction of a fool really is something else. I don’t hate that about you, though.”
“I am not a fool, indeed! Only fools call people fools, you fool! Idiot!”
“Fufu… truly foolish. I suppose this is when you’d say the foolish child is the cutest one of all.”
Shut up, indeed! Stop looking at me with those gentle eyes, indeed!
“Wha—!? Don’t tell me you’re after my behind!? No thank you, indeed!”
Being dug into by the Spear Spirit is something I refuse, indeed!

“Well, there are times I think about finally going through with it. I could use you as an axle for a wheel, after all. Unfortunately, the structure doesn’t allow for that anymore, which is a real shame.”
This homo spirit! Absolutely the worst, indeed. Haven’t you had your fill digging into Takt already, indeed!?
“Well, the moment I chose you and started lending you power, one could already say I’d been digging into you in a sense.”
“Stop it, indeeeeeeeed!”
I have not been dug into, indeed! I’ll turn you into an axle even harder, indeed!
“Cut out the psychological attacks, indeed! No matter what, I will never give up, indeed!”

“I’m not particularly trying to make you give up on anything. It’s just that there’s so much I can only tell you in a place like this—rather troublesome. Especially given there are people who can actually hear my voice.”
“I know nothing of that, indeed!”
“Well, fine then. Anything else you want to know… there were some companions this time around that don’t usually show up in other loops, you know.”
“Wolf, perhaps?”
“That’s right. All sorts of outcomes from his actions. The Claw Spirit was fairly satisfied with him.”
“Claw is a fickle one, indeed. Claw belongs to Filo-tan, indeed.”
“From your perspective maybe, but I think showing some masculine spirit like that isn’t a bad thing.”
He’s exclusively Filo-tan’s, indeed.
“Well, the Claw Spirit is something close to a primal weapon, so a lot of people tend to be compatible with it. Those who carry something wild in them especially tend to be chosen easily.”
Come to think of it… the Spear Spirit said, sounding as though something had just occurred to it.

“Master Ark mentioned this too, but the weapon that the demon girl made first ended up becoming the easiest vessel for a spirit to dwell in… but it seemed like he’d noticed something. That guy’s always so suggestive about it… what does he know, what did he notice, I wonder?”
“I wouldn’t know that either, indeed.”
I refuse to believe there’s someone out there even more suggestive than you, indeed.
“Anyway, it’s dwelling in Filo’s hand too, so he’s always right there in the good spots, that guy.”
So don’t ask me to agree with that, indeed.
“Given the flow of this conversation, it’d feel wrong to leave out the one you call Crocodile Guy, so let me tell you a bit about him too.”
“Is there something to tell, indeed?”

“Well, the same goes for Rabbit Guy, Theodore, but it turns out there’s a certain cause-and-effect—a fate somewhat favorable to our side—that only becomes clear later. Like with Raphtalia-chan’s ancestors, or Atla-chan and Fohl. Though to be blunt, the location where the first Wave was triggered was rather pinpoint, in a sense.”
Crocodile Guy is essentially from the same homeland as Big Sister, in practical terms, indeed.

“He apparently served as the very first attendant to follow the Shield Hero. Different jurisdiction from mine, but… well, it seems pretty certain that the mastermind behind the Waves was working in the shadows behind his species’ extinction.”
“The Crimson Swine again, indeed? Is all the misfortune in this world her doing, indeed?”

“Probably. Let’s see… you wouldn’t remember this, but there’s a line reincarnators and Heroes sometimes use sarcastically—‘why doesn’t the Demon Lord just kill the Hero first? It’s strange not to kill them while they’re still weak, right?’ But if you think of it as the Demon Lord literally putting in serious effort from the start to crush the Hero, it’s not so strange after all, is it?”
“What an unpleasant comparison, indeed.”
We got thoroughly beaten down by the Crimson Swine’s own preparations, indeed. Even game knowledge turned out to be dangerously wrong in places, indeed.
“Maybe he’s actually… hmm.”
“What about Crocodile Guy, indeed?”
“No, even I can’t quite see through it… there’s definitely something there, but it’s even harder to pin down than with Theodore.”
“How is it that Rabbit Guy is easier to figure out, indeed?”
“Because his origin is a spirit, and moreover—that’s something I’d rather not say, and it’s not relevant anyway.”
Stop with that kind of implication, indeed.
“Instead, let me tell you a little story about Master Ark.”
“That was a suspiciously abrupt change of subject, indeed.”

“Just listen. About that terrifying second generation who raised an adopted child—when he became a spirit, he ended up the husband of someone truly incredible. Top tier among top tiers—the Spirit Divine Beast, a god among spirits.”
“Oh… indeed. Hm?”
Something about that is nagging at me, indeed.
